az_waves_of_rock.blurb: Waves of Rock is a large, easily spotted slab on the southwestern side of the Granite Basin area near Prescott. A gully divides the formation into two slabs. It holds six routes, mostly two pitches long, with grades from about 5.4 up to 5.8, which makes it a gentle place for newer leaders and first multi-pitch outings. Expect smeary slab climbing rather than steep pulling. At least some lines are fully bolted with two-bolt anchors, while others suit a trad rack. A walk-off down the right side of the slab, with second- and easy third-class steps, brings you back to the base.

az_waning_wall_the.blurb: The Waning Wall is a traditional cliff roughly 100 feet tall in the Granite Gardens section of the Granite Dells, just outside Prescott. It has six routes from 5.5 to 5.8, a mix of lead lines and top-rope options. This is not a bolted crag: fixed anchors are scarce, just a couple of old pitons and a single bolt, with nothing on top, so you must build your own. Several lines have awkward gear and run-outs, which suits experienced trad climbers more than beginners. The way down is a walk-off with some scrambling. The dirt road to the crag leaves the east side of Highway 89.

az_yarnell_wall.blurb: Yarnell Wall is a remote, southwest-facing granite face in central Arizona, near the town of Yarnell. The main face is about 55 meters tall and mixes slab with steeper slab, plenty of cracks and a band of overhangs near the top. Six traditional routes climb it, mostly 5.8 and 5.9 with one or two harder, including two-pitch lines on a standard rack. Expect an adventurous, quiet outing with room for new lines rather than a crowded cragging day. The walk in is long, about a couple of hours each way along a memorial trail and an old mining road.
az_yarnell_wall.parking_note: Leave the car at the Granite Mountain Hotshot Memorial trailhead off Highway 89, then follow the memorial trail.

az_stella_stone.blurb: Stella Stone is a small boulder in the Panther Peak bouldering area on the west side of the Tucson Mountains, roughly half an hour from downtown Tucson. It is a sunny, flat-topped block holding six easy problems, from very easy up to V1, so it works as a warm-up stop before the bigger lines nearby. The rock is the volcanic pebbly conglomerate found across the area, which varies widely in quality. To find it, follow the trail toward the Monkey Skull boulder; Stella Stone sits just downhill and west of the Little Bug Boulder, with a slightly overhung arete on its left side.

az_riven_wall_the.blurb: The Riven Wall is a north-facing granite wall on Little Granite Mountain, in the McDowell-Sonoran Preserve at the edge of Scottsdale. It gets shade in the afternoon and is easy to recognize by its broken face. Six routes mix trad, one sport line and one top-rope, with grades running from about 5.5 to 5.7, so it suits newer climbers happy to place gear. The wall has no fixed anchors, so bring what you need to build them. The descent is an easy walk-off. The surrounding mountain is a desert area of coarse granite with a traditional feel.
